profile.name: Scott Moss
profile.tagline: AI engineer, focused on AI safety research
profile.description: Scott Moss is an AI engineer focused on AI safety research. He shares what he learns and helps startups and enterprises adopt AI.
intro: I’ve built AI systems at {netflix} and as a two-time {yc} founder. Now my focus is AI safety research: how these systems fail, how to measure them and how to make them safe.
As an applied AI architect, I also help startups and enterprises adopt AI, from choosing the right problems to systems that hold up in production. And I create content sharing what I learn.

items.name: Direction
items.about: A Mac app for making films the way directors do. You write the brief, circle the takes you want and give notes in plain language, like “let it breathe” or “too many star shots.” An AI editor, Claude Code or Codex, cuts the film, answers every note in the next cut and delivers the master, a web copy and captions. You never touch a timeline. It’s open source.
items.why: I make a lot of video, and editing was always the bottleneck. I knew how I wanted a film to feel, but getting there meant hours in a timeline. I built Direction so I could stay in the director’s chair and hand the editor’s job to an agent. It’s also a real test of how far you can trust an agent with creative work.
